one_liner: In-place, allocation-light C++ XML DOM parser with XPath 1.0, beating libxml2 on parse throughput.
what_it_does: pugixml parses XML into an in-memory DOM-like tree (xml_document/xml_node/xml_attribute) and offers a near-complete XPath 1.0 engine for queries over that tree. It is not a drop-in for libxml2: the object model, naming, and error handling (xml_parse_result, optional exceptions) are pugixml's own, though it supports std::string/string_view and STL streams. It is a non-validating parser — no DTD or XML Schema validation, and only predefined entities are expanded.
how_it_is_fast: Node and attribute names/values are pointers into a single large parsed character buffer rather than individually heap-allocated strings; the fastest load path (load_buffer_inplace/_own) parses the caller's buffer directly ('in-situ' parsing), avoiding the extra copy libxml2's DOM path makes. Tree storage uses its own page-based allocator (one big allocation) instead of many small node allocations, and the recursive-descent parser uses lookup-table character classification rather than generic, more DTD/encoding-aware machinery. An optional compact mode trades ~10-50% more CPU time for 2.5x-5x smaller tree memory via relative-offset node/attribute encoding.
when_to_use: Parsing well-formed XML (config files, save formats, scene/asset descriptors) in the 1-20MB range where DOM parse throughput matters and libxml2's generality is overhead you don't need
Embedding in game engines or tools that want a small, dependency-free, MIT-licensed C++ XML library (two source files, or header-only via PUGIXML_HEADER_ONLY)
Need XPath 1.0 queries and in-place tree editing without pulling in libxml2's full XPath/validation stack
Memory-constrained targets where compact mode's 2.5x-5x smaller tree is worth a 10-50% parse-time cost
Codebases spanning C++98 through C++20 that want one parser across that range (move semantics and range-for activate automatically under C++11, string_view under C++17)
when_not_to_use: Need DTD or XML Schema validation, or custom (non-predefined) entity expansion — pugixml explicitly does not do this
Documents too large to fit fully in memory — pugixml is DOM-only, no incremental/SAX streaming mode
Want a drop-in libxml2 replacement — the API surface, error model, and node types are different, so this is a rewrite, not a swap

Need the benchmarked numbers to be independently reproducible: the comparison lives in a chart-rendering script (benchmark-data.js) on pugixml.org, not a runnable harness in the repo or a public benchmark repo under the author's account

Targeting strict-alignment architectures with very old pugixml versions — a misaligned-access UB bug in UTF-16/32 decoding was reported and fixed (issue #698, closed 2026-04-14); make sure you're on a version at or after that fix

integration.form: source-drop (src/pugixml.hpp + src/pugixml.cpp, ~2 files); header-only build available via PUGIXML_HEADER_ONLY
integration.dependencies: none required; STL usage is optional and can be disabled with PUGIXML_NO_STL
integration.min_toolchain: C++98 minimum; C++11 unlocks move semantics/range-based for; C++17 unlocks std::string_view overloads and optional charconv float formatting (PUGIXML_CHARCONV_FLOAT)
integration.platforms: any (portable standard C++, no SIMD/arch-specific code path)
integration.thread_safety: Free (non-member) functions are safe to call from multiple threads; concurrent read/write is safe as long as each tree is only accessed from one thread at a time; concurrent access to the same tree from multiple threads needs external synchronization; set_memory_management_functions is not thread-safe (per docs/manual.adoc, 'Thread-safety guarantees').
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different API (xml_document/xml_node vs libxml2's xmlDoc/xmlNode) and different error-handling model; no compatibility shim

gotchas: load_buffer_inplace/_own parse by modifying the caller's buffer in place; the buffer must outlive the document tree, and load_buffer_inplace does not take ownership (you must free it yourself)
The non-inplace load_buffer copies the input into a private buffer first, which costs more time and memory than the inplace variants — use inplace when performance is critical
No DTD/XML Schema validation and no custom entity resolution; only the five predefined XML entities are expanded, unresolvable references are left as-is
Whole document must fit in memory — there is no streaming/SAX-style incremental parse mode
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick pugixml over roxmltree when the codebase is C++ (roxmltree is Rust) and you need in-tree mutation plus XPath 1.0, not just read-only access; pick it over stb_xml when you need XPath, Unicode encoding conversion, or DOM editing rather than a minimal single-header reader. The HTML-focused siblings (lexbor, html5-parser, MyHTML, selectolax, MarkupEver) target malformed/HTML5 markup, not well-formed XML, so they solve a different problem.
verified_claims_summary: On an Intel Core i7 @ 2.67GHz with MSVC 2015 ('all optimizations on'), pugixml parsed nine 1-20MB XML test files (including a 10MB XMark file) into a DOM 4.5x-23.4x faster than libxml2's DOM mode and 2.7x-19.1x faster than libxml2's SAX mode on x86 builds, with similar 4.1x-24.1x / 2.6x-19.7x ratios on x64; the figures come from pugixml.org's benchmark-data.js chart data rather than a public, runnable benchmark harness.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-06-16, current release 1.16, CI on GitHub Actions/AppVeyor, MIT-licensed, not a fork or archived); small enough (two source files) to vendor directly into a project.
